name: 方壶胜境 Fanghu Shengjing
line: The towers on their terraces over the water as the leaf of 1744 paints them and S01 draws them: nine two-storey towers in three ranges (S05, S361, Malone), the lower terrace with its stepped bastions on the water, the upper brick-faced terrace, the galleries joining the towers' upper floors, the causeway with its two archways to 迎薰亭 and the two cruciform terraces with 集瑞亭 and 凝祥亭; S01 gives the layout (B), the leaf the storeys, roofs, colours and parts (A for 1744), the texts the names; every height, every bay's width and the ornaments are C.
rows: As S01 draws it, re-read in Round 24 in plan pixels (B): the lower terrace on the water and its bastions, the upper terrace behind it, three ranges each of a five-bay middle block and two side towers, the galleries, the strips out to the two cross terraces, the causeway and the square terrace; the bastions' line matches the ruin's today (P0383, P0787)
The inlet the terraces stand in (S01; the leaf), water in the ground since Round 24 (W0365; Q191); its level the rule of Round 10 (C)

The front range: five bays on two floors (S05 上下各五楹, A), a skirt roof and a balcony between them, 歇山 in yellow tile with green trim, red columns and lattice (the leaf, A for 1744); the three-bay entry before it, one storey under the upper floor's balcony (S01, the leaf; bays C); the plaque 方壶胜境 over its door (S05; board C)
锦绮楼 and 翡翠楼 (the 1740 plaques, S310; which is which C): two storeys, 歇山 with their gables to the water, yellow with green trim (the leaf); S01's blocks

On the upper terrace (Malone: brick-faced; S05 其北樓宇為噦鸞殿): five bays on two floors, 歇山 in purple-brown tile with green trim (the leaf; Q175); 碧云楼 and 紫霞楼 either side, joined by two-storey galleries (Malone's elevated walks)

At the back (S05 又北為瓊華樓): five bays on two floors under a double top eave, yellow with blue trim (the leaf); 千祥阁 and 万福阁 either side, purple-brown with green trim and two tiers of eaves (the leaf); galleries joining them and running down the court's sides to the middle range (S01, Malone); a terrace behind (S01's rectangle, C)

Flagged; bronze vessels and potted flowering trees before 哕鸾殿 (the leaf; their number and places C); the stair on the axis from the lower terrace (S01; its steps C); the walls round the upper terrace, red with yellow coping, a gate in the west and east walls (S01; colour C; 蕊珠门 is one of the 1740 plaques)

The galleries on their strips out to two stepped cross terraces (S01; Malone: a bridge and two piers to three small terraces) with 集瑞亭 and 凝祥亭: a lower eave and a cross-ridge 十字脊 roof, blue with yellow trim (the leaf); the causeway with two archways 坊座 (S05; places and form C) to the square terrace of 迎薰亭: double eaves, a yellow pyramid roof with a gilt finial (the leaf), four bronzes, two dragons and two phoenixes (E1856; form C), three flights to the water for the barge (S01, Malone)

Every height (the terraces 2.6 and 1.9 m above the water, the upper terrace 3.0 m above the lower, the storeys 3.6 and 3.2 m), every bay's width, the galleries' width and form, the archways, the bronzes, the vessels and trees, the walls' colour, the rear terrace: the hall kit's classes and the Qing manual's typology (C, the pale tint with conf=1). No dig and no Yangshi Lei sheet with figures has been seen (Q119, E1855)
